evidence_note: Cases catalog the book claims in own words; many rest on informants and inference, so each case keeps its gaps visible.

cases.name: Astor
cases.pattern: Rise through lodge access and state privilege into fur, opium, land, and banking, then influence through press, foundations, and transatlantic institutions.

cases.name: Bundy
cases.pattern: Adviser, intelligence, and foundation placement, with a manufactured problem and managed solution used as the model case.

cases.name: Collins/Todd
cases.pattern: Hidden occult authority with council imagery, witness intimidation, and a prison-framing narrative showing retaliation against exposure.

cases.name: DuPont
cases.pattern: Dynastic secrecy, press management, cousin marriage, chemical monopoly, and state capture in one small state.

cases.name: Freeman/Prieure
cases.pattern: A guarded bloodline order with archives, grand-master succession, and presidential advisers as hidden instruction channels.

cases.name: Kennedy
cases.pattern: Surname frequency blocks simple identification, so the search shifts to intermarriage clusters and aristocratic branches.

cases.name: Li/Triad
cases.pattern: Territorial factions with public covers, strong-arm units, extortion, and infiltration of police and government.

cases.name: Onassis
cases.pattern: Shipping wealth and social access read as power channels, with sparse direct ritual evidence admitted in the text.

cases.name: Rockefeller
cases.pattern: Layered trusts and foundations funding seminaries, universities, media, and religious bodies into alignment.

cases.name: Rothschild
cases.pattern: Five brother-led houses in major capitals, family-only partnership, private couriers, coded correspondence, and finance as control over governments.

cases.name: Disney
cases.pattern: A wholesome family brand allegedly lowering audience guard, with a wordless music film catalogued as a foundation template case at abstract level only.

cases.name: Reynolds
cases.pattern: Foundation grant networks and interlocking directorates linking tobacco, banking, aluminum, and universities.

cases.name: McDonald
cases.pattern: Clan continuity claims and franchise diffusion, with a documented compensation report used as an evidence exhibit.

cases.name: Krupp
cases.pattern: Concealed rearmament through foreign front companies, scandal suppression, and trial reversal by an insider.

gaps: Many claims rest on confidential interviews, unnamed informants, or inference rather than documents shown in the text.
Namesake ambiguity affects several family cases; similar surnames are not proof of relation.
OCR noise makes some names, figures, and dates unreliable as extracted.
Ritual descriptions are fragmentary: roles and symbols appear without procedures, durations, or safeguards.
Internal article page numbers restart; PDF page markers are the reliable locator.
